evals.prompt: Show me the brain by lobe so I can rotate it and name each one: the four lobes, the insula, the cerebellum and the brainstem. One HTML file I can open offline, light theme.
evals.expected_output: The response takes the 3D route (it says so, and says it takes minutes, not an Epic) with BodyParts3D as the atlas. It runs scripts/atlas.mjs bp3d --find for each requested name, writes a truth.mjs whose PARTS have atlas ids and the atlas's own names (right and left lobes as one row with two ids; the brainstem as midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata, or as one brainstem mesh if the user wanted one part, and says which), fetches and packs the meshes into examples-style meshes/*.json with a LICENCE.md, and writes a build.mjs from the brain example. The delivered light page is one standalone HTML file with a WebGL canvas in the framed card: drag turns it, it opens anterior forward and superior up, each lobe is in its own tissue tone, hovering a part lights it and writes n · Name in the readout, arrows step the parts in key order, Q hides the names, and numbered tags sit on their own parts. The key under the card lists every part, every one of the nine (frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital lobes, insula, cerebellum, midbrain, pons, medulla oblongata) by number and name, generated from truth.mjs, and the caption cites BodyParts3D 4.0, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP and the fetch date. checkTruth passes, scripts/view-check.mjs prints view-check: ok, and the front, left and top were captured and read against the atlas before delivery.

evals.prompt: The hippocampus with the amygdala, fornix and parahippocampal gyrus around it, in 3D so I can see how they sit. Dark theme, one HTML file.
evals.expected_output: 3D route, BodyParts3D (human). atlas.mjs bp3d --find confirms hippocampus, amygdala, fornix of forebrain and parahippocampal gyrus; truth.mjs has four rows with those ids and the atlas's names, the fornix in the tract tone, the amygdala in the nucleus tone, the hippocampus in its own tone, the gyrus in the cortex tone. One dark standalone page, one card: all four parts in the key by number and name, generated from the truth table; the figure opens from a view that shows the hippocampus (FRAME.open, from above-left, since the amygdala hides it from the front); hover names each part; arrows step with the stepped part lit and the rest dimmed, never transparent; Q hides the names; the caption cites BodyParts3D and its licence. The response says what the atlas does not have: no human hippocampal subfields (CA fields, dentate gyrus) as meshes, and offers a drawn coronal section on the section route if the user wants them. checkTruth passes and view-check prints ok.

evals.prompt: Show me the limbic system in 3D so I can see how the parts fit together. Light theme, one HTML file.
evals.expected_output: 3D route, BodyParts3D, one card, and the response says it takes minutes. atlas.mjs bp3d --find confirms each member: hippocampus, fornix of forebrain, mammillary body, thalamus, hypothalamus, amygdala, cingulate gyrus and parahippocampal gyrus; truth.mjs has one row per member with its atlas id and the atlas's name (the fornix named Fornix, with fornix of forebrain kept in atlas.names), tones by class: the hippocampus in its own tone, the fornix in the tract tone, the mammillary body, thalamus, hypothalamus and amygdala in the nucleus tone, the two gyri in the cortex tone. One light standalone HTML file whose title says limbic system and human: every member in the key by number and name, generated from the truth table; hover names a part; arrows step with the stepped part lit and the rest dimmed, so each part can be found among the others; Q hides the names; the caption cites BodyParts3D 4.0, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP and the fetch date. Before building, the response says which standard members it left out or the atlas lacks (the septum is in the atlas as septum of telencephalon and can be added; the anterior thalamic nuclei are not separate from the thalamus), and that the Papez circuit's pathways are not drawn in 3D and would be a section figure. checkTruth passes, view-check prints ok, and the front, left and top were captured and read against the atlas.

evals.prompt: The basal ganglia, how they fit together around the thalamus, for my exam. Dark theme, one file I can open offline.
evals.expected_output: 3D route, BodyParts3D, one card. Before any geometry the response says which members the atlas has and lacks: the caudate nucleus, putamen and globus pallidus are in it, and the thalamus; the substantia nigra, the subthalamic nucleus and the nucleus accumbens are not. truth.mjs has four rows (caudate nucleus, putamen, globus pallidus, thalamus) with atlas ids and the atlas's names, in the nucleus tone. One dark offline HTML file whose title says basal ganglia and human: the four parts in the key by number and name, generated from the truth table; hover names, arrows step with the rest dimmed, Q hides the names; the caption cites BodyParts3D 4.0 and its licence and names the two missing nuclei, the substantia nigra and the subthalamic nucleus, so the key is not read as the whole system. Nothing is drawn by hand for the missing parts. The response offers the direct and indirect pathways as a section figure (a Hero) if the user wants the circuit, not in 3D. checkTruth passes, view-check prints ok, three captures read against the atlas.

evals.prompt: Make me a figure of a pyramidal neuron with the three glial cell types around it, with every part labelled so I can test myself: soma, dendrites, axon hillock, axon, myelin sheath, nodes of Ranvier, axon terminals, astrocyte, oligodendrocyte, microglia. Dark theme, standalone HTML.
evals.expected_output: The response takes the section route and says why: no atlas has a neuron or its glia as meshes. It sizes it as a Figure (30-90 minutes). A dark standalone isometric page of a neuron on a stand with a truth.mjs listing the ten parts the user named verbatim, in the user's order, SOURCE.convention set to the user's list, and sources fetched only for borders and connections. The soma is a sphere or lathe, dendrites are routes that leave it tangent and branch at ball tees, the axon hillock tapers, the axon is one route with myelin collars gapping it and bare nodes between, terminals end on balls, and each glial cell is its own body whose processes end on something (the neuron, a collar, a capillary). One pin per part, every one of the ten parts in the key by number and name, generated from the truth table, quiz mode working (Q hides names, click reveals). checkTruth passes, --audit ends audit passed, line ends: 0, 4x close-ups of every end and collar in both themes were read.
